prerequisites: Manufacturing methods (turning, milling, drilling... Cutting tools, cutting parameters, tooling)

learning_outcomes.text: To identify and compare different robotized manufacturing strategies.
To evaluate the potential benefits of robotized manufacturing strategies.
To take into account the technical and organizational constraints linked to their implementation in an industrial environment.

syllabus_topics: Articulated robots (6 axes) for complex 3D machining and FSW welding
SCARA robots for high-precision assembly in electronics
Parallel robots (Delta) for fast pick-and-place operations
Collaborative robots equipped with force sensors for finishing operations

Robotic manufacturing operations (Hybrid operations combining machining and inline quality control, Friction stir welding (FSW), Intelligent completion with 3D vision and AI systems, Machine tool loading/unloading with automatic tool management)

Robot programming (Off-line programming with software such as NX CAM for preliminary simulation, Direct teaching via touch pendulums for fine adjustments, Adaptive programming using force/torque sensors for machining, Pre-optimized motion libraries for FSW)

Implementing robotic manufacturing (Analysis of process constraints, Design of modular cells with standardized interfaces, Integration of vision systems and IoT sensors, Validation by digital twin before deployment)
Critical points (Robot/effector suitability for FSW, Vibration management in robotic machining, Securing material flows in cells)
Case study: Completion and FSW welding (Application Airbus, Solution Proxinnov)
Application TP (Inverse kinematic modeling of a 6-axis robot, Programming machining trajectories on a complex part, Implementation of FSW parameters, Metallographic analysis of welded joints)
degree: Titre d'ingénieur ENIT (cycle ingénieur, semestres 5-10; orientación mecánica/producción)
